title: Why the Men of Jabesh-Gilead Risked Their Lives for Saul’s Body
paragraphs: Why the Men of Jabesh-Gilead Risked Their Lives for Saul’s Body
There are moments in Scripture that feel too human to be invented.
Moments where broken men carry the weight of memory deeper than fear.
And buried in the ashes of Saul’s tragic downfall is one of the most emotionally devastating acts of courage in the entire Old Testament.
Men who walked through the darkness of enemy territory… risking torture, execution, and humiliation… just to recover the mutilated body of a fallen king.
A king who died in fear.
A king whose final chapter looked like disgrace.
Yet they still came for him.
And once you understand why… this story becomes one of the deepest pictures of covenant memory, gratitude, honor, redemption, and the terrifying cost of loyalty.
Most people read this account quickly.
But if you slow down long enough… it feels less like ancient history and more like the story of every person who has ever wondered:
“Will anybody still come for me after I fail?”
Israel has collapsed under Philistine attack.
Mount Gilboa has become a graveyard.
Israel’s first king has fallen by his own sword.
The Philistines strip Saul’s armor, cut off his head, and fasten his body to the wall of Beth-shan as public humiliation.
“Then the valiant men arose and walked all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan; and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.”
The Hebrew phrase for “valiant men” is:
This does not merely mean brave men.
It carries the idea of men of strength, substance, valor, moral force, military courage, and noble character.
These were men who understood exactly how dangerous this mission was.
Saul’s body was displayed as a political trophy.
To retrieve it meant entering hostile territory under the cover of darkness.
Because decades earlier… Saul had done something nobody else would do.
To understand Jabesh-Gilead’s loyalty, you must return to 1 Samuel 11.
Before Saul became corrupted by jealousy.
There was a city crying for help.
Nahash the Ammonite surrounded the city and offered horrifying terms of surrender.
“On this condition I will make a covenant with you, that I may thrust out all your right eyes, and bring reproach on all Israel.”
The Hebrew expression here is deeply violent.
Ancient warfare understood the right eye as strategically important for combat because shields often protected the left side while the right eye guided attack.
Nahash was not merely threatening pain.
He was planning permanent humiliation and military crippling.
“And the Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard those tidings, and his anger was kindled greatly.”
“The Spirit of God rushed powerfully upon him.”
Because many only remember Saul’s collapse.
But there was a time when God genuinely empowered him.
A time when Saul fought for the helpless.
A time when Saul delivered the oppressed.
A time when Saul looked like the king Israel hoped for.
But some people never forget the person who came for them when nobody else would.
That is what makes this story so emotionally devastating.
When Saul died… most of Israel ran.
They remembered the day Saul saved their families from mutilation and shame.
And now the man who once rescued them hung publicly dishonored.
There is something deeply Christlike hidden in this story.
Because the Gospel itself is the story of Someone who came for dishonored people.
The Apostle Paul writes in Romans 5:8:
Jesus came for humanity while humanity was spiritually hanging on the wall of shame.
And this is why the story of Jabesh-Gilead grips the human heart.
Because every soul longs for someone who will still come after failure.
Someone who will not define us only by our worst chapter.
Saul’s life became tragic because partial obedience eventually becomes total destruction.
That is one of the terrifying theological truths of Saul’s story.
Religious appearance without surrender eventually collapses.
Saul wanted kingdom benefits without fully submitting to God’s authority.
And many people today are trying to do the same.
They want the crown without repentance.
But Saul’s story warns us that hidden rebellion eventually becomes public ruin.
Yet even in Saul’s collapse… grace flickers through the darkness.
Because God allowed men from Jabesh-Gilead to preserve Saul’s dignity after death.
Even David later honors their actions.
“Blessed be ye of the LORD, that ye have shewed this kindness unto your lord, even unto Saul, and have buried him.”
The Hebrew word for “kindness” here is:
One of the most powerful covenant words in the Old Testament.
The men of Jabesh-Gilead showed chesed.
And Scripture remembers them forever because of it.
There are people reading this right now who secretly believe their failures have erased every good thing God ever did through them.
You remember your collapse more than your calling.
Your shame more than your purpose.
Your weakness more than His mercy.
But one of the stunning truths of the Bible is that God tells stories honestly.
Scripture does not hide Noah’s drunkenness.
Because the Bible is not propaganda.
And revelation tells the truth about humanity.
The truth that all have sinned.
The truth that unchecked flesh consumes.
But also the truth that God still moves toward broken people.
Some of the most dangerous spiritual words a person can say are:
The cross already settled how far God is willing to go to rescue sinners.
In Aramaic, one of the cries associated with Jesus on the cross is:
“My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
Matthew 27:46 preserves this cry because heaven wanted humanity to understand the cost of redemption.
Jesus entered abandonment so sinners could enter reconciliation.
He entered shame so believers could receive righteousness.
He entered death so humanity could receive eternal life.
And unlike Saul… Christ is the King who never failed.
The King who does not merely rescue Jabesh-Gilead.
This is why the Gospel is not self-improvement.
Somebody reading this has been carrying hidden shame for years.
But privately you feel spiritually nailed to the wall.
You wonder if anybody would still come for you if people knew the whole story.
But Jesus specializes in walking into impossible places to recover what looked lost forever.
And this article is not an accident.
God may be confronting something buried deep inside you right now.
One path leads deeper into darkness.
And only one of those paths ends in life.
This hit harder than you expected.
Your honesty may become the testimony that helps somebody else return to God.
Some people only love you while you are winning.
Jesus loved you knowing every chapter you would fail.
Bakit Isinugal ng mga Lalaki ng Jabesh-Gilead ang Kanilang Buhay Para sa Bangkay ni Saul
May mga bahagi ang Biblia na parang hindi gawa-gawa lamang.
Mga tagpong may mga lalaking pasan ang bigat ng alaala nang higit pa sa kanilang takot.
At sa gitna ng madilim na pagbagsak ni Haring Saul… may isang kwento ng katapangan na halos hindi nabibigyan ng sapat na pansin.
Hindi ito kwento ng mga propeta.
Hindi ito kwento ng mga hari.
Hindi ito kwento ng mga tanyag na mandirigma.
Ito ay kwento ng mga lalaking hindi nakalimot.
Mga lalaking naglakad sa dilim… tumawid sa teritoryo ng kaaway… handang mamatay… para lamang kunin ang katawan ng isang bagsak na hari.
Isang haring ang huling kabanata ay puno ng kahihiyan.
Pero pinuntahan pa rin nila siya.
At kapag naunawaan mo kung bakit… mararamdaman mong hindi lang ito kasaysayan.
Parang kwento ito ng bawat taong natatakot na baka wala nang babalik para sa kanila pagkatapos nilang magkamali.
Patay ang mga anak ni Saul.
At ang unang hari ng Israel ay bumagsak sa sarili niyang espada.
Pagkatapos noon, pinutol ng mga Filisteo ang ulo ni Saul at isinabit ang kanyang katawan sa pader ng Beth-shan bilang pampublikong kahihiyan.
“Lahat ng magigiting na lalaki ay tumindig at naglakad buong gabi, at kinuha ang bangkay ni Saul at ang mga bangkay ng kanyang mga anak mula sa pader ng Beth-shan.”
Sa Hebrew, ang salitang ginamit para sa “magigiting na lalaki” ay:
Ibig sabihin nito ay mga lalaking may dangal, lakas ng loob, moral na tibay, at tapang na handang mamatay para sa tama.
Dahil maraming taon bago bumagsak si Saul… siya ang taong dumating para iligtas sila noong walang ibang gustong tumulong.
Bago pa nasira si Saul ng inggit.
Bago siya naging suwail sa Diyos.
Napapalibutan noon ang Jabesh-Gilead ng mga Ammonita.
At ang kanilang hari na si Nahash ay nagbigay ng nakakakilabot na kondisyon:
“Papayag lang ako kung bubunutin ko ang kanang mata ng bawat isa sa inyo.”
“At sumakanya ang Espiritu ng Diyos nang may kapangyarihan.”
“Makapangyarihang dumating sa kanya ang Espiritu ng Diyos.”
Dahil maraming tao ang si Saul lang na bumagsak ang naaalala.
Pero may panahon na tunay siyang ginamit ng Diyos.
May panahon na ipinaglaban niya ang mahihina.
May panahon na iniligtas niya ang mga desperado.
At hindi iyon nakalimutan ng Jabesh-Gilead.
Pero may mga taong hindi nakakalimot sa taong dumating para sa kanila noong wala nang iba.
Kaya nang mamatay si Saul… habang tumatakbo ang iba… may mga lalaking naglakad papunta sa panganib.
Hindi nila naalala ang kabaliwan ni Saul.
Hindi nila naalala ang pagseselos niya kay David.
Hindi nila naalala ang kanyang pagbagsak.
Naalala nila ang araw na may isang hari na tumayo para sa kanila.
At ngayon… ang haring iyon ay nakasabit sa pader sa kahihiyan.
Walang kasiguraduhan kung mabubuhay pa sila.
At may mas malalim pang dahilan kung bakit napakalakas ng kwentong ito.
Tayong lahat ay parang si Saul.
Mga taong may kasalanang hindi maitago.
At si Jesus ang Hari na dumating para kunin tayo mula sa espirituwal na kahihiyan.
“Subalit ipinakita ng Diyos ang Kanyang pag-ibig sa atin, na noong tayo’y makasalanan pa, si Cristo ay namatay para sa atin.”
Iyan ang klase ng pag-ibig ni Cristo.
Maraming tao ang naniniwalang ang kanilang pagkakamali ang katapusan ng kanilang kwento.
Pero ang Biblia ay paulit-ulit na nagpapatunay na ang Diyos ay lumalapit pa rin sa mga wasak.
Si Pedro ay itinanggi si Jesus.
Si David ay nagkasala nang malalim.
Pero ipinapakita ng Kasulatan ang katotohanan dahil ang Biblia ay hindi propaganda.
At ang rebelasyon ay nagsasabi ng katotohanan tungkol sa tao.
Na kayang sirain ng pride ang tao.
Na ang lihim na rebelyon ay nagiging pampublikong pagkawasak.
Pero ipinapakita rin nito na mas malalim ang biyaya ng Diyos kaysa kasalanan ng tao.
May taong nagbabasa nito ngayon na pagod na.
Pagod nang ngumiti habang wasak sa loob.
At baka pakiramdam mo… kapag nalaman ng tao ang totoo tungkol sa iyo… wala nang babalik para iligtas ka.
Pero si Jesus ay espesyalista sa paglapit sa mga lugar na puno ng kahihiyan.
Siya ang Hari na bumababa para kunin ang mga nawawala.
At baka hindi aksidente na binabasa mo ito ngayon.
Baka may bagay na matagal mo nang tinatago.
At ngayon… tinatawag ka ni Cristo na sumuko.
Mas tumama ito kaysa inaasahan mo.
Ang testimony mo ay maaaring maging dahilan para may isang taong bumalik kay Jesus.
May mga taong mahal ka lang kapag malakas ka.
Pero minahal ka ni Jesus kahit alam Niya lahat ng pagbagsak mo.
